graph.title: Arduino Zero Simple Audio Frequency Meter
notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. None were added or dropped.
Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue: bank 't' is rows a-e, which are the lower half of the image. Bank 'b' is rows f-j, the upper half.
Top rail row 'tp' is the +supply and bottom rail row 'bn' is GND, as drawn in the image.

The op-amp is placed with pin 1 (OUT1) in column 14 of row e and pins 5-8 in row f. The Fritzing image matches this: the brown A0 wire and the purple wire meet at column 14, and the VCC wire lands on 14b.

Circuit, taken from the schematic: IOREF (3.3 V) powers the op-amp VCC and R8, the 100k divider top. R8 and R9 bias IN1+. C1 AC-couples the jack signal into IN1+, and the jack sleeve goes to GND. R11 (47k) and the trimmer form the feedback path from OUT1 to IN1-, and R10 (47k) goes from IN1- to GND. OUT1 goes to A0.

The 10k trimmer is wired as a variable resistor between R11 and OUT1. SIG is the wiper, joined to OUT1 by the purple wire. VCC is joined to R11 at column 3. GND is left unconnected. This matches the schematic, where R7's other end is open.

I could not read the right-hand end of the green jumper on row C from the image. I put it at column 15, the IN1- pin, because the schematic needs IN1- tied to the R10/R11 junction. Column 14 would short the output to the inverting input.
I joined the 'jack signal' wire to jack pin RING1, the schematic's RIGHT contact. TIP (LEFT) is not connected.
The second op-amp (IN2+, IN2-, OUT2) is unused and its pins are not wired. The schematic leaves them open.
The 100 nF capacitor uses the generic non-polar capacitor-22pf type with value=100nF, because the catalogue has no 100 nF type.
